Any correlation is dominated by macro noise. There is no credible mechanism translating a Rubio odds change into a same-day S&P move of meaningful size.

llm_justification.summary: The market concerns who wins the 2028 US presidential election, focused on Marco Rubio. This is a very long-dated political question with no plausible mechanism to move liquid public markets within a 12-hour window. Even a large probability swing would carry negligible actionable information for equities, FX, or commodities today. We map this to broad US equities only as a nominal proxy with 'unclear' direction and near-zero expected move — well below the 700bps tradable threshold. This is a null/weak-signal case.
key_assumptions: No imminent real-world catalyst (announcement, scandal) is driving the move
Markets do not discount 2028 electoral outcomes in intraday pricing
Prediction-market probability changes here are largely noise
failure_modes: A genuine breaking news event (e.g., Rubio candidacy declaration or major scandal) could give the move real content we mislabel as noise
Sector-specific bets (defense, immigration-exposed names) could react more than the broad index, making SPY a weak proxy
The move may simply reflect thin-market repricing with no informational value
Direction is inherently ambiguous — a Rubio win could be read as market-neutral or mildly pro-business, so even the sign is unknowable at 12h
